messages:
maya: quick idea — thinking about surfacing a "fallback probability curve" in the rollout editor so operators can see how small threshold tweaks change expected fallback rate (:chart_with_upwards_trend:). want quick feedback.
alec: can you sketch the problem we're solving? is this for daily ops or during canaries?
maya: both. operators currently pick a single threshold (e.g. 0.8 confidence) and hope. we have no intuitive hook for how changing that number affects volume, latency, or cost. curve would show probability vs threshold + estimated token impact.
zhen: love it. also we should link each point on the curve to sample traces and the audit event stream — so you can click and inspect why a request would fallback.
devon: fwiw, we'd need percentile bands (p50/p95) for latency on the same plot or a small panel. cost delta is key for product owners.
sam: how does this interact with per-route overrides vs global fallback policies? we already have a lot of confusion there.
maya: plan: show base (global) curve and overlay per-route curve when route has overrides. UI toggles. also allow simulated rollouts that apply a candidate policy against recent traffic.
alec: +1 for simulate. if simulate uses sliding window traffic we can show expected number of users affected and give a confidence interval
eva: can we present a short "why fallback" tooltip per sample? e.g., cookie of conditions that matched: error-class, latency, model-variant-unavailable.
maya: yes — show compact audit card: source, rule, matched-signal, hit-ts, trace-id. something like:
```
policy: auto-fallback-v2
trigger: latency_ms > 1200 OR error_code IN [502,503]
decay: 0.6 (15m)
estimated_fallback_rate@threshold=0.7 -> 3.6% (±0.5)
```
ops-bot: incident-note: last week we had a burst of 502s in eu-west-1; any UI that surfaces sensitivity to 502 spikes will help ops :+1:
deploy-bot: figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/fallback-curve-proto — has a compact sim panel and audit card (comments on the right)
zhen: telemetry needs: link to sample ids, ability to jump to trace and to playback request with original prompt (redact PII obviously). also store the simulation seed so audits are reproducible.
alec: API debate: should simulate call the existing /policies/simulate endpoint or a new /rollouts/simulate that returns UI-shaped telemetry? prefer reuse but add a UI view model on top.
sam: edgecase: what about probabilistic fallbacks? curve needs to represent stochastic policies (drawn %). maybe show expected % and variance.
devon: UX idea: small "what-if" slider that adjusts threshold and shows live numbers (estimated tokens, latency delta, fallback count). keep it keyboard friendly.
maya: next steps: i'll update figma with a simulate button and that audit card, zhen can draft the telemetry fields we need, alec pls call out whether simulate should reuse existing API. i'll follow up with a short PR to the rollout API docs.
alec: will do. can we add a small mock endpoint response example for the UI? e.g.
```
{
  "threshold": 0.7,
  "estimated_fallback_rate": 0.036,
  "token_delta": 12000,
  "samples": ["trace:abc123", "trace:def456"]
}
```
eva: nice. one more thing — include a "why changed" blurb when overlaying global vs route curves so PMs understand override impact.
maya: sweet. thanks all. tagging @devon @zhen for implementation sync tomorrow at 10am.
